correctness.rationale: Every quantifier is explicit: primes p>=13 and arbitrary A of strictly more than half the nonzero squares. Cauchy--Davenport gives |2A|>p/2 when p=1 mod4. For p=3 mod4, Vosper reduces a possible failure to an arithmetic progression; direct quadratic-character pair correlations give T_epsilon=(p-5-2chi(2))/8, strictly less than its requisite m-1 triples for p>=19. Exact examples establish the sharp exceptional orders at p7,p11 and necessity of order four at p13. Code exhausts 24275 finite cases but is not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The problem is the natural local additive-basis threshold for the sparse quadratic-residue set motivated by a contemporary 10-summand theorem. The conclusion gives a structural and quantitative improvement to four summands for all primes >=13, isolates exactly two exceptional primes among p>=7, and establishes sharpness at p13 using a concrete obstruction; this is a finite-field structure theorem with a nontrivial character-sum/Vosper boundary, not a routine parameter substitution.
